title: LedgerFlow: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Receipt Roll. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Logo spirit, Orvect ergonomics (numbered steps, language switch EN/FR/SV, outlined controls, honest states) and the trilingual agent are fixed in every option.

options.label: The Receipt Roll
options.lineage: Swedish card-terminal thermal receipts, perforated roll paper, the BOKFÖRD rubber stamp
options.thesis: Every receipt prints its own proof: a paper strip unrolls line by line as LedgerFlow reads, posts, runs and verifies, and tears off at the perforation when a human signs the exact file.
materials: cool thermal paper strips with zigzag tear edges
thermal fade from grey to black
options.viewport: iPhone home: wordmark and EN/FR/SV switch on top; a live paper strip fills the upper half, printing the latest receipt's real status lines (READ · POSTED · RUN · VERIFIED · BOKFÖRD); a large camera shutter docked bottom-centre. First launch: a numbered 01–04 how-it-works strip that prints itself, screen by screen.
options.risk: Thermal paper can drift into cream nostalgia: it must stay cool, crisp and data-true, and the printing motion may only ever print real events, never fake progress.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: the total prints at display size, every other line in small mono.
Length is time: the strip only grows when a real execution event arrives, so its length is the run's honest timeline.
Rendering is a state: lines print faded grey until the verifier confirms them, then re-print in full black.
On the Mac, the run you are reviewing lifts and the rest of the queue dims.

options.label: The Ledger Grid
options.lineage: the spreadsheet itself: cell addresses, the selection rectangle, the formula bar
options.thesis: The cell is the brand: LedgerFlow speaks in cell addresses and selection rectangles, and every screen shows exactly which cells a receipt will change.
materials: selection rectangle with a corner handle
options.viewport: iPhone home as a single living sheet: the last receipt's eight cells highlighted in their rows, a formula-bar line explaining the entry, the shutter button as the active cell.
options.risk: Familiar: every spreadsheet product looks like a grid; it can read as an Excel clone and says little about the receipt or the proof.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.lineage: wide-margin reference editions with a keyed centre rail
options.thesis: Receipt and workbook as twin columns around a centre rail of numbered keys: each key is a pipeline step, ruled at one device pixel.
options.viewport: Mac review: receipt left, cell changes right, the rail of steps 01–06 down the middle with detents for each verified check.
options.case: Fuses well on the Mac review screen (product clarity holds); loses on audience identification for the phone-first employee.
options.risk: Reads academic and slow on a phone; small type fights the camera-first task.

options.label: Crouwel Grid
options.thesis: The workbook grid as visible construction: big figures built cell by cell, the grid toggled on as a real state.
options.viewport: iPhone home: the month's total assembled from grid cells, the scan action as the one accent plane.
options.case: Accountants identify with the grid (audience axis holds); the receipt-to-proof story gets lost (clarity loses).
options.risk: Becomes a type poster rather than a bookkeeping tool.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: nobody books receipts by dragging a weight axis.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone (raised into The Receipt Roll).

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.case: Fuses poorly: notation is foreign to finance staff.
options.kept: Length encodes duration (raised: the strip grows only with real events).

options.label: Emigre Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Fuses partly (receipts are dot-printed) but legibility of amounts suffers.
options.kept: Rendering as an honest state (raised: faded until verified).

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.case: Fuses poorly: receipts are not entertainment posters.
options.kept: Focused item lifts, the rest dims (raised into the Mac queue).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fintech expense app, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, monthly spend card, big scan button, recent expenses list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Pleo, Expensify and the accounting suites by design.
